chunks: From him, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from his father, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I have land subject to land tax (kharaj), and I have grown weary of it; should I leave it?' He was silent from me for a moment, then said: 'Indeed, our Qa'im (the Awaited Imam), peace be upon him, if he had risen, would have given you from the land more than it is.' And he said: 'And if our Qa'im, peace be upon him, had risen, it would be for the people better than their land plots (qata'i).'
ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the land tax (kharaj) and the coming of the Qa'im?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) uses a moment of contemplative silence before responding, highlighting the gravity of the Qa'im's eschatological reign. He reassures the narrator that the Mahdi’s rule will not merely alleviate the current Umayyad/Abbasid land tax (kharaj) but will generate such divine abundance that the burden becomes negligible. This underscores the Shia belief in the Qa'im’s role in establishing economic justice and material prosperity that surpasses contemporary feudal land holdings (qata'i).
